paper_title: Realizing the efficiency-stability balance for all-polymer photovoltaic blends

qa_pairs.question: What are the components of the one-pot synthesized PM6-b-PY-IT multicomponent system?
qa_pairs.answer: The PM6-b-PY-IT system is a multicomponent material consisting of the donor polymer PM6, the acceptor polymer PY-IT, and a block copolymer in which the PM6 donor and PY-IT acceptor blocks are chemically bonded together.
qa_pairs.source_title: Realizing the efficiency-stability balance for all-polymer photovoltaic blends

qa_pairs.question: How does the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of the PM6-b-PY-IT system compare to the binary PM6:PY-IT blend?
qa_pairs.answer: The binary PM6:PY-IT blend achieves a higher PCE of 15.24%, whereas the one-pot synthesized PM6-b-PY-IT multicomponent system reaches a lower PCE of 13.63%.
qa_pairs.source_title: Realizing the efficiency-stability balance for all-polymer photovoltaic blends

qa_pairs.question: What specific photovoltaic parameters contribute to the lower efficiency of PM6-b-PY-IT compared to the PM6:PY-IT binary blend?
qa_pairs.answer: The efficiency drop in PM6-b-PY-IT is primarily due to a lower short-circuit current density (JSC) of 21.51 mA cm-2 and a lower fill factor (FF) of 68.2%, compared to the PM6:PY-IT blend's JSC of 22.60 mA cm-2 and FF of 72.2%.
qa_pairs.source_title: Realizing the efficiency-stability balance for all-polymer photovoltaic blends

qa_pairs.question: What does the ideality factor (n) indicate about the recombination mechanisms in PM6-b-PY-IT solar cells?
qa_pairs.answer: The PM6-b-PY-IT system has an ideality factor (n) of 1.20, which is higher than the 1.13 observed for the PM6:PY-IT blend. This indicates that PM6-b-PY-IT-based devices suffer from higher levels of trap-assisted bimolecular recombination.
qa_pairs.source_title: Realizing the efficiency-stability balance for all-polymer photovoltaic blends

qa_pairs.question: Why does the PM6-b-PY-IT system exhibit lower hole and electron mobilities than the PM6:PY-IT blend?
qa_pairs.answer: PM6-b-PY-IT shows lower hole mobility (8.18 × 10^-4 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1) and electron mobility (4.67 × 10^-4 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1) likely because the donor–acceptor alternatively connected block structure prompts limited bi-continuity and reduced phase purity in the film.
qa_pairs.source_title: Realizing the efficiency-stability balance for all-polymer photovoltaic blends

qa_pairs.question: Describe the device architecture used to evaluate the performance of PM6-b-PY-IT and PM6:PY-IT.
qa_pairs.answer: The devices utilized a conventional architecture with the configuration: ITO/PEDOT:PSS/active layer (polymer blend)/PDINN/Ag.
qa_pairs.source_title: Realizing the efficiency-stability balance for all-polymer photovoltaic blends

qa_pairs.question: Based on GIWAXS analysis, how does the crystallinity of PM6-b-PY-IT differ from the PM6:PY-IT blend?
qa_pairs.answer: GIWAXS analysis shows that the PM6-b-PY-IT system has lower overall crystallinity and shorter crystalline coherence lengths (CCLs) for π-π packing in both directions compared to the binary PM6:PY-IT blend.
qa_pairs.source_title: Realizing the efficiency-stability balance for all-polymer photovoltaic blends

qa_pairs.question: Compare the operational photostability of PM6-b-PY-IT and PM6:PY-IT under 1 sun illumination.
qa_pairs.answer: The PM6-b-PY-IT system demonstrates significantly better operational stability with a T80 value (time to reach 80% of initial PCE) of 681 hours, whereas the PM6:PY-IT binary blend has a lower T80 value of 416 hours.
qa_pairs.source_title: Realizing the efficiency-stability balance for all-polymer photovoltaic blends
